solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Food brought up from the mouth

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a child brought up is one bred

explanation.surface: Something disgusting: food regurgitated from the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: BRED (brought up) sounds just like the staple food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is a basic baked staple, a classic example of food.

clue.text: Bad forefather is recollected in family group?

indicators.note: collected again, re-gathered into a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked ancestor is remembered within the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' reads as remembered, but splits as re-collected: the letters are gathered anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of a feather are people of the same kind who flock together, like a family.

clue.text: What may come from the dictator?

definitions.text: What may come from the dictator?

indicators.note: the letters can be taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking what a tyrant might issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters sit in thE DICTator, and a dictator issues decrees.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree, the kind of order a dictator issues.

clue.text: Damper spot had to be blasted

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A damp spot had to be blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damper' looks like 'more damp' but is a noun, a device that damps motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashpot is a mechanical damper that resists motion using fluid friction.

clue.text: A very quiet artist is a learner being examined by supervisor?

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: An art student is being quietly assessed by a supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: being examined by your boss is undergoing an appraisal, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a formal review of an employee's performance by a manager.

clue.text: Sailors said to follow a classical hero

indicators.note: means the sailors come after the a
spoken, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: jacks, as in jack tars, are sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors are said to follow a hero of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a Greek warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Chum with misstep involved in a sort of cover-up

parts.note: a pal is a chum

indicators.note: entangled, so the letters are twisted together

explanation.surface: A friend's blunder gets him caught up in hushing something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover-up' is literal: a palimpsest is a manuscript with new writing over scraped-off older text.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest's original text is overwritten by later writing, a sort of concealment.

clue.text: Something deemed medicinal I understand and must swallow

indicators.note: taking something in, so it goes inside

parts.note: 'I see' means I understand

explanation.surface: Someone understands they must swallow a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed has long been used as a herbal remedy, for coughs and digestion.

clue.text: Trader in railway location, one down the line from Victoria

parts.note: a station is a stop on a railway

parts.words: one down the line from Victoria
parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a descendant of Queen Victoria

explanation.surface: A trader sets up at a station down the line from London Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the London station, but it is the Queen: Elizabeth II is in her line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a retailer who sells paper, pens and office supplies.

clue.text: College man on TV right to pull apart council admin, say

indicators.note: pulling something apart breaks it up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic on television is right to criticise council administrators.
explanation.definitionFit: Local government is the system of councils running a district's affairs.

clue.text: Put back controls, seemingly unbelievable

parts.note: reins are what control a horse
a tall story is one that seems unbelievable

explanation.surface: Someone restores controls that had seemed unbelievable.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall something is to fit or set it up again in its former place.

clue.text: Sarah's boy is a Bill

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated AC

explanation.surface: Sarah says her son is called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Sarah is the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Isaac is the son born to Sarah in her old age.

clue.text: Arguments going the wrong way I'd avoided in organisations

indicators.note: the letters of I'd are kept out, i.e. dropped from the word
travelling backwards, so the word for arguments is read from its end

parts.note: disputes are arguments

explanation.surface: Arguments turn sour, and someone avoided them within their organisations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' turns DISPUTES into SETUPSID; 'avoided' then removes ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-ups are arrangements or structures, as in an organisation or company.

clue.text: Claim of fairy alone, not one seen as "queenly"

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth, who might claim 'I'm peri'

indicators.note: means the word one is left out of the word alone

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairy claims to be on her own, and not regal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' removes ONE from ALONE, leaving AL. A peri is a fairy in Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means relating to an empire or an empress, so majestic and regal.

clue.text: Nerve needed by head of board when acquiring fuel

indicators.note: the nerve comes first, followed by the head

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
DG, director-general, heads a board such as the BBC's
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A chairman needs nerve when buying fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled gas, such as propane or butane, is a fuel sold in cylinders.

clue.text: Regard admissions of debt as flippant

parts.note: a regard, as in 'in that regard', is a facet or aspect
IOUs ('I owe you') are written admissions of debt

explanation.surface: Someone takes acknowledgements of debt lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regard' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, an aspect: in that regard, in that facet.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious describes treating serious matters with inappropriate humour.

clue.text: Oppressed group of workers (excellent/no good?) in endless reorganisation

indicators.note: placed inside the other word
without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a change is a reorganisation
the final letter of the word for reorganisation
A1 means excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: Downtrodden workers, rated excellent or useless, face constant restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash reads like a choice between two verdicts, but both halves supply letters: A1 is old slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a group of convicts chained together to do hard labour.

clue.text: Wild animal behaving with love to the end

indicators.note: means the letter for love is shifted to the final position

parts.note: doing, as in 'what are you doing?', means behaving
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A wild creature acts lovingly right to the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the end' moves the O of DOING to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is Australia's feral wild dog.

clue.text: Loud day of religious rejoicing — no hesitation to provide a banquet

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

indicators.note: means the hesitation sound is taken away

parts.note: Easter Day celebrates the Resurrection
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A noisy religious holiday is celebrated without delay with a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no hesitation' removes ER from EASTER, leaving EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large, lavish meal, the same as a banquet.

clue.text: Short school period to accommodate every one individually — so I work less?

indicators.note: holding something within, so it goes inside
cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
the last letter of the school period
each means every one considered separately

explanation.surface: Short school terms take in each pupil, so the narrator works less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts TERM to TER, which holds EACH. The definition is cryptic: the answer is one who teaches, so the pupil, the 'I', may slack off.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher does the instructing, so a pupil with a teacher might hope to do less work.

clue.text: Time to demand church to form working group

parts.note: to ask for something is to demand it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Time is up: the church is demanding a working group be set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a unit formed for a specific job or operation.

clue.text: Rubbish in lean period halved, a good deal being kept

indicators.note: held within, so it goes inside
only half of the word is used, its last three letters cut away

parts.note: a famine is a lean time of scarcity
the second half of the word for lean period
lots means a good deal

explanation.surface: In a lean time, rubbish is cut by half, much of it held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' keeps the first half of a six-letter word for a lean period.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage or debris, by extension worthless rubbish.

clue.text: One toughening up an item for the pew, we hear

indicators.note: says the words are judged by how they sound when said

parts.note: an gives AN; a kneeler is the cushion knelt on in a church pew

explanation.surface: Something placed in a church pew to toughen people up.
explanation.walkthrough: A kneeler is a hassock, the cushion kept in pews for kneeling in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Annealing heats and slowly cools metal or glass to make it tougher and less brittle.

clue.text: Leaving home to be entertained by wine supply expert

indicators.note: being hosted by something means being inside it

parts.note: a wine bin is where bottles are stored
someone off is leaving, going away from home

explanation.surface: A wine expert is entertained by the cellar on leaving home.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical specialist.

clue.text: Style is something flashy, reportedly

indicators.note: as it is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a flare is a sudden bright flash of light

explanation.surface: Style is defined as being a bit showy, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair means stylishness or natural elegance and talent.

clue.text: Deep fish

explanation.walkthrough: The two words are separate meanings of one word, with different pronunciations.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass is both the lowest musical range and a type of perch-like fish.

clue.text: PM shown as pagan type when passing on measure

indicators.note: passing on something means doing without it, so it is removed

parts.note: a heathen is a pagan
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister appears to be a pagan when he declines a measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath served as Conservative Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Good girl battling against male's ultimate fiascos?

parts.note: a lass is a girl
being at war is battling

indicators.note: the final letter of male, the word it is attached to

explanation.surface: A good girl fights against a man's final disasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiascos' looks like disasters, but a fiasco is also an Italian wine flask, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiaschi, straw-covered wine bottles, are items made of glass, so are examples of glassware.

clue.text: Girl falling short is sort to trouble pedants

indicators.note: troubling stirs things up, so the letters are mixed
stopping one letter early, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the final letter of Girl

explanation.surface: A girl not quite up to it is the sort to annoy fussy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts GIRL to GIR; 'to trouble' rearranges GIR, IS and SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigorists insist on strict observance of rules, like pedants.

clue.text: Give weary maiden backing to achieve a good grade

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to tire is to make or become weary
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Supporting a tired young woman so she can get a high mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A merit is a grade awarded for good work, just below distinction.
